newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo says "ashamed" of government.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo says "ashamed" of government.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, reacting to the arrest of a one-time top aide, said Wednesday he was "ashamed" of having been a minister in the government.

Cavallo, who has embarked on a fierce anti-corruption crusade since being fired by President Carlos Menem in July, went to Buenos Aires international airport to greet the former head of the nation's customs service.
Since his dismissal by Menem, Cavallo has launched himself as an alternative political force, though he plays down the likelihood he will run for the nation's presidency in 1999.
He has unleashed a battery of corruption accusations against the government and judiciary. He has also been enmeshed in a series of court cases for his graft-related comments.
A judge ordered the arrest of Parino on the weekend in connection with a probe into an organized smuggling ring. As head of the customs service, he had reported to Cavallo when he was minister.
But Gustavo Parino was arrested on arrival in the country as part of a smuggling probe and was barred from talking to his ex-boss.

A furious Cavallo told reporters" "I am ashamed of having been a minister in this country with a lack of security and where the highest officials have no dignity. As I have been able to witness tonight, when I tried to greet a gentleman, an innocent person who is being persecuted and is a political prisoner."

Cavallo said earlier this week that both he and Parino were the targets of persecution by the courts, which he claimed were being manipulated by "mafias" trying to protect themselves from his campaign against corruption.

Cavallo backed down Tuesday on his earlier insinuations that Menem had some knowledge of alleged bribes paid to win a $250 million contract with state-owned Banco Nacion, saying "I am not going to implicate President Menem with corruption."
But he repeated accusations against Corach, Menem's chief of staff Alberto Kohan and Justice Minister Elias Jassan, saying "Hopefully the president has decided to fire those criminals."
Cavallo has accused Corach and Jassan of manipulating judges. He also says that Kohan knew of but failed to act on Banco Nacion bribes.
Corach is suing Cavallo for slander.
Attending a meeting of the Mercosur trade bloc in Brazil, Menem and Kohan avoided commenting on Cavallo. Jassan's office said he had no comment.
